The big picture

Gary and Anna leave Phoenix on September 1 and don't touch back down until the 27th — 27 days, three countries, six changes of address. The first two weeks are the Cyclades: Athens bookending a run of ferries between Santorini, Paros and Mykonos. Then a flight north for a week at Oktoberfest in Munich, overlapping Pat's own trip for four nights. The last stop is unexpected but real: three nights in Boston's North End before the flight home.

This page is the companion to the Munich Oktoberfest guide — same trip family, Aegean colors. Everything here reflects the confirmed calendar: dates, hotels, and the transportation and beach recommendations built out leg by leg.

A few things are still open — a couple of exact addresses, a dinner reservation, whether one short island hop is a flight or a ferry. Each is flagged where it comes up.

Golden rule

Santorini's caldera stairs are the hardest terrain of the whole trip — take the Fira cable car, not the 300 steps, and budget bottled water everywhere on the island; tap water isn't potable.

Sep 3–5, then Sep 16

Athens

The Athens Gate Hotel faces Hadrian's Arch, a five-minute walk from the Acropolis's south entrance. Athens bookends the island run — a proper visit on arrival, then a short overnight near the airport on the way to Munich.

Sunrise at the Acropolis
Go at opening — heat, crowds, and slippery marble all get worse as the day goes on.
Pestemal shopping at maresi
After 11am, Adrianou 100 in Plaka — the walk down from the Acropolis lines up naturally.

Sep 5 – 16

Santorini, Paros & Mykonos

Santorini (Oia)

Home in Oia, private rental · arrive by flight from Athens
• Caldera stairs are the hardest terrain on the trip — take the Fira cable car, not the 300 steps.
• Drive or bus to Ammoudi rather than walking down.
• Tap water isn't potable (desalinated) — buy bottled. Carry coins for public toilets.
LAUNDRY — no self-service on the island
Eco Cleaners / Laundry Spa (Kamari) covers Oia with pickup & delivery. +30 6943474729. Wash around Sep 8–9, late in the stay.
Open — no restaurant chosen yet for the caldera sunset dinner (reservation recommended in September).

Paros

Studio Orion, Allparos Villas — $408.88 · arrive by ferry from Santorini
Kolympithres — signature granite-boulder coves with pool-like inlets, calm and shallow. Near Naoussa.
Golden Beach (Chrysi Akti) — long dune beach, the island's most popular, reliable wind for windsurfing.
Santa Maria — long white sand, full amenities, easiest "show up and relax" option.
Open — exact Allparos Villas address isn't confirmed, so the closest beach can't be pinned down yet.

Mykonos

Olia Hotel, Tourlos — $538.88 · arrive by ferry from Paros
Tourlos is a port/marina area, not a beach base — plan a short taxi south to Chora's beach strip.
Ornos — closest well-organized option, ~2.5 km from Chora. Calm, family-friendly.
Psarou — a short hop further, upscale/celebrity beach, calm water.
Platis Gialos — 4 km from Chora, resort feel, easy boat taxis onward to Paradise/Super Paradise.
For the livelier scene: Paradise and Super Paradise, worth booking loungers ahead in September.

* For comparison — see the note below on why this leg is very likely a flight, not a ferry.
What the calendar's identical 50-minute windows suggest

All three inter-island transit entries show the same 11:00am–11:50am block. That's realistic for exactly one: Paros → Mykonos on the fastest SeaJets catamaran. Santorini → Paros needs 1.5–2 hours minimum, so that entry is likely a placeholder. Mykonos → Athens has no ferry under ~2 hours 50 minutes — the strongest evidence that leg is a flight, not a ferry, especially since Alekos Luxury Suites is described as near the airport, not near Piraeus port.

Sep 17 – 24

Munich & Oktoberfest

Athens to Munich, depart 12:45pm, arrive 2:30pm on Sep 17. JAMS Music Hotel for the week — six of seven nights fall inside Oktoberfest 2026 (Sep 19 – Oct 4), and the last four nights overlap Pat's own stay. Full tent-by-tent detail, restaurant picks, and the day-by-day plan live on the companion Oktoberfest guide — this section covers just what's specific to Gary & Anna's arrival.

MUC Airport → JAMS Music Hotel

S8 S-Bahn to Rosenheimer Platz, then a 4-minute walk to Stubenvollstraße 2 — the same route as Pat's own stay. About 35–45 minutes door to door. Single ticket €15.10; group day ticket €32.60 for up to 5 people.

LAUNDROMAT — Sep 17 or 18

City Dry Clean Waschsalon, Rosenheimer Str. 103 — 9-minute walk from JAMS. €4.50 wash, €2/10 min dry. Do it on arrival or the morning after, before any tent night.

Sep 24 – 27

Boston

A late add to the trip

The original brief called Boston out of scope — the trip calendar shows real dates and a booked Airbnb in the North End, so it's back in. Depart Munich 12:10pm, arrive Boston 7:50pm on Sep 24.

Sep 27 — depart Boston 10:35am, arrive Phoenix 1:10pm. Trip complete.

Sound like a local

Greek phrases & etiquette

Καλημέρα
Kalimera — good morning
Γεια σου
Ya sou — hi (informal)
Γεια μας!
Yamas — cheers, to our health
Ευχαριστώ
Efharisto — thank you
Παρακαλώ
Parakalo — please / you're welcome
Πόσο κάνει;
Poso kani? — how much is it?
Ώπα!
Opa! — an exclamation of joy
Την υγειά μας
Tin eyia mas — to our health, a toast
A few notes: tipping isn't obligatory but rounding up or leaving 5–10% is appreciated; a small nod or "efharisto" goes a long way. Siesta hours (roughly 2–5pm) mean many small shops close — plan errands around it. For the German phrases needed in Munich, see the companion Oktoberfest guide.
Καλό ταξίδι!

Bon voyage, Gary & Anna — 27 days, three countries, six stamps in the passport. The full Word itinerary and slide deck live alongside this page in the Greece folder; the Munich crossover pairs with the companion Oktoberfest guide.
